title: Senegal's Oil and Gas: 36.2m Barrels, a Woodside Arbitration, a Modest Budget Line | The Six, Ep. 26
lede: Senegal's Sangomar field produced 36.2 million barrels of oil in 2025, and the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim gas project shipped about 18.5 LNG cargoes in its first year. The government is reviewing the contracts, Woodside has taken a tax dispute to arbitration, and oil and gas still bring in under 2% of budget revenue.
keyPoints: Sangomar, operated by Woodside (82%) with state company Petrosen (18%), began production in June 2024 and produced 36.2 million barrels in 2025; output averaged 99,000 barrels a day in the first half of 2026 and 94,000 in the third quarter (Reuters; Woodside via Seneweb).
The bp-operated Greater Tortue Ahmeyim LNG project, shared with Mauritania, shipped about 18.5 cargoes in 2025 and targets up to 36 in 2026; Petrosen holds 10% (MSGBC; JPT).
Woodside filed for ICSID arbitration on May 30, 2025 over a CFA41 billion (about $68 million) tax reassessment; Woodside says it acted in line with applicable regulations (Ecofin; bne IntelliNews).
Under the 2024–2026 finance laws, oil and gas revenue net of the state's equity costs is 1.1% to 1.6% of budget revenue; NRGI projects a peak of about 5.5% in 2029 (NRGI, June 2026).
2026 debt service is projected at CFA5,497.9 billion, close to 93% of budget revenue (NRGI).
